CITY OF ALHAMBRA
  NOTICE OF SPECIAL MEETING OF THE
  ALHAMBRA CITY ARTS AND CULTURAL EVENTS COMMITTEE
  CORONAVRIUS (COVID-19) ADVISORY NOTICE
Consistent with Executive Orders No. N-29-20 and No. N-35-20 from the Executive Department of the
State of California and the County of Los Angeles Department of Public Health Safer at Home Order,
the Alhambra City Arts and Cultural Events Committee will not be physically open to the public and
will take place via video conference.
To watch and listen to the meeting: To maximize public safety while still maintaining transparency
and public access, members of the public can participate by using Zoom Meeting as follows:
Zoom Meeting direct link:
https://us02web.zoom.us/j/84117364416?pwd=RG4wSC9SbVFraTNkRGxkby9YYTNVUT09
For those wishing to speak on an agenda item, please e-mail Kelsey Rivadeneyra at
kelsey@cityofalhambra.org prior to the meeting with the item number you wish to speak on and your
name. You should then join into the meeting using
https://us02web.zoom.us/j/84117364416?pwd=RG4wSC9SbVFraTNkRGxkby9YYTNVUT09,
Meeting ID: 841 1736 4416, and Passcode: 693422 or 833 548 0276 US Toll-free, 833 548 0282 US
Toll-free, 877 853 5257 US Toll-free, 888 475 4499 US Toll-free 10 minutes prior to its start time.
Ms. Rivadeneyra will announce to you when it is your time to speak. You will have five minutes to
speak, unless that time is adjusted by the President.
As an alternative you can e-mail your comments by sending them to kelsey@cityofalhambra.org no
later than 5:00 P.M. on March 17, 2021 to ensure that it will be printed prior to the beginning of the
meeting. Comments will then be read into the record, with a maximum allowance of 5 minutes per
individual comment, subject to the President’s discretion. If a comment is received after 5:00 P.M. but
before the conclusion of the meeting based on its time stamp, the comment will still be included as a
part of the record of the meeting but will not be read into the record.
Any member of the public who needs accommodations or who needs their comments translated should
e-mail or call Kelsey Rivadeneyra at kelsey@cityofalhambra.org or (626) 570-5044 who will use their
best efforts to provide reasonable accommodations to provide as much accessibility as possible while
also maintaining public safety. Given the challenges of video conference meetings, all participants are
encouraged to e-mail their comments prior to the beginning of the meeting.
  KELSEY RIVADENEYRA

  CLERICAL ASSISTANT II

Dated: March 9, 2020

   CITY OF ALHAMBRA

 II.  FLAG SALUTE

 V.  PUBLIC COMMUNICATION
  Discussion from the public of any item not specified on the agenda. Comments must pertain to

VI.  COMMITTEE COMMUNICATION
  Discussion from the Committee Members of any item(s) not specified on the agenda. Items

Copies of staff reports or other written documentation relating to each type of business described herein above are on file in

City Arts and Cultural Events Committee  Action Item III
  APPROVE

  MINUTES
  ALHAMBRA CITY ARTS AND CULTURAL EVENTS COMMITTEE
  Wednesday, September 16, 2020
  7:00 P.M.

The regular meeting of the City Arts and Cultural Events Committee was called to order at 7:02
P.M. on Wednesday September 16, 2020 at Alhambra City Hall, 111 South First Street
Alhambra, via Video Conference Zoom.

ROLL CALL
Committee Members Present: Canseco Chan, Luthi, Rutkowski and Zeller.
Committee Members Absent: None.
Also attending: Deputy Director Brie Houghton and Clerical Assistant II Kelsey Rivadeneyra.

APPROVAL OF MINUTES OF THE OCTOBER 16, 2019 MEETING
On the motion of Canseco Chan and with a second by Zeller, the minutes of the June 17, 2020
Meeting were unanimously approved as written.

ELECTION OF OFFICERS FOR 2020/2021 TERM
President Canseco Chan
Vice President Camille Rutkowski

STAFF REPORT
City Arts and Cultural Events Committee reviewed and discussed a Tournament of Roses
Bloomfest 2021 PowerPoint Presentation. Bloomfest is a floral sculpture exhibition that offers
the beauty and creativity of the Rose Parade’s iconic floats to a drive-by audience craving the
fun, familiarity, and flowers that hundreds of thousands of Southern Californians anticipate each
year. On a motion of Luthi and with a second by President Canseco Chan, the City Arts and
Cultural Events Committee agreed to not proceed with investing and participating in BloomFest.

PUBLIC COMMUNICATION
None.

COMMITTEE COMMUNICATION
President Canseco-Chan inquired if any of the City Arts and Cultural Events committee
members planned to participate in the Hispanic Heritage Scavenger Hunt event and how the
public has responded to the event. The committee discussed and collectively agreed that it is a
fun organized event to bring together the community while maintain safety protocols. Deputy
Director Houghton asked the committee if they knew any artists that are interested in exhibiting
their art in the Alhambra City Hall Lobby for 2021 since there are some vacancies.
 ADJOURNMENT
President Canseco-Chan moved to adjourn the City Arts and Cultural Events Committee Meeting.
Seconded by Vice President Rutkowski, the meeting was adjourned at 7:24 P.M.

Unofficial until adopted by the  April 21, 2021
City Arts and Cultural Events Committee  Action Item III
  APPROVE

  MINUTES
  ALHAMBRA CITY ARTS AND CULTURAL EVENTS COMMITTEE
  Wednesday, March 17, 2021
  7:00 P.M.

The regular meeting of the City Arts and Cultural Events Committee was called to order at 7:01
P.M. on Wednesday March 17, 2021 at Alhambra City Hall, 111 South First Street Alhambra,
via Video Conference Zoom.

ROLL CALL
Committee Members Present: Canseco Chan, Sanchez, and Zeller.
Committee Members Absent: None.
Also attending: Director Michael Macias, Deputy Director Brie Houghton and Clerical Assistant
II Kelsey Rivadeneyra.

APPROVAL OF MINUTES FROM THE SEPTEMBER 16, 2020 C.A.C.E. MEETING
On the motion of Canseco Chan and with a second by Zeller, the minutes of the September 16,
2020 City Arts and Cultural Events Committee meeting were unanimously approved as written.

STAFF REPORT
Deputy Director Houghton informed the committee about upcoming special events scheduled for
the spring. On March 25, 2021, Car Bingo will take place at the Joslyn Senior Center and the
$5.00 admission includes a pack of 10 games, 1 dauber, and light refreshments. From March 1-
26, 2021, the Eggstravagant Egg Decorating will be open to the public and submissions of Easter
egg drawings will be displayed in the City Hall Lobby Art Gallery. In addition to the display,
there will also be an Egg Guessing Game placed in the lobby that participants can guess using
the provided QR code or with paper and pen. From March 19 – April 5, 2021 the Spring Egg
Scramble will be open for participants to hunt for the large Easter egg cut out placed on the lawn
at each Alhambra park and on the cut out will be a game piece that the participant can put it into
the egg scramble game to decode a hidden message. Every submission will receive an Easter
basket prize.

Deputy Director Houghton informed the committee there are two vacancies in the 2021
Alhambra City Hall Lobby Art Gallery calendar- August and October. She then asked if the
committee knew any artists that would be interested in exhibiting either this year or the next.

President Brian Canseco-Chan replied that he has an friend in mind that would be interested in
exhibiting in the Alhambra City Hall Lobby for October 2021 and that he would contact him
after the meeting to discuss further.
 At this time, the Tournament of Roses and City of Pasadena are in the process of arranging plans
and protocols for their 2022 parade. Director Michael Macias informed the committee that the
City of Alhambra plans to participate in the 2022 parade and will use the 2021 chosen art contest
winner and float design since the theme “Believe, Dream, Achieve” from their cancelled 2021
parade has been reissued.

PUBLIC COMMUNICATION
None.

COMMITTEE COMMUNICATION
Committee member Sanchez inquired if any developments had occurred during the past month
with the Raising Cane’s art project. Deputy Director Houghton replied that their Art in Public
Places application was disqualified due to their art (two arrow shaped drive-through entrance and
exit signs) not meeting requirements.

President Canseco Chan would like to establish an art alley behind the businesses on Main Street
with murals painted by local artists and art pieces suspended above the walkways. Committee
member Sanchez supports the idea and mentioned that she has enjoyed a similar display of
public art in the City of Riverside where umbrellas hung above the walkways in an artistic
fashion. She shared an idea of distributing tiles to the community that could be hand painted and
then arranged into a large collage by artists as a possible public art installation in the proposed
art alley.

On the motion of President Canseco-Chan and with a second by Sanchez, the Art Alley Project
will be on the April 2021 City Arts and Cultural Events Committee agenda.

ADJOURNMENT
Zeller moved to adjourn the March 17, 2021 City Arts and Cultural Events Committee Meeting.
Seconded by Vice President Sanchez, the meeting was adjourned at 7:31 P.M.
